Newly appointed CEO John Ternus reportedly plans to "completely overhaul" Apple, aiming to make the company "faster and leaner." Bloomberg cited sources saying measures include launching more products and cutting "middle management positions."

John Ternus wants to reshape Apple — here's his reform plan

First, the new Apple CEO hopes to launch more products faster than before, including becoming "bolder in experimentation." One idea is to break Apple's traditional spring and fall release rhythm, instead rolling out new products more evenly throughout the year.

Ternus also wants to "build a leaner, more engineering-focused organisational structure," which involves multiple cost-cutting and restructuring measures. One change is "eliminating some middle management positions to reduce layers between engineers and senior leadership."

Reports indicate that Apple's hardware engineering division has laid off "a batch of engineering project managers (EPMs)" over the past two weeks. Bloomberg described these positions as "the core of Apple's product development process for decades," responsible for "managing timelines and coordinating work across teams."

The report stated: "Those affected include several project managers, of whom approximately six are at the director level — one of the company's most senior staff ranks." "They were given only a few weeks to find other positions internally at Apple; employees who fail to transfer will be laid off later this year."

However, Bloomberg noted that cost-cutting actions may expand further. Ternus has reportedly long advocated that Apple should be more "lean":

In addition, Apple reportedly shelved a plan this summer to cut 5,000 AppleCare employees because they believed AI-driven customer service agents could handle the related work.

At the same time, Ternus hopes to work with Eddy Cue and CFO Kevan Parekh to boost Apple services revenue. The report stated: "They have discussed launching new services and extracting more revenue from existing products and businesses."
